Backend/IaC release: the 3 Function Apps, portal (frontend + backend), and
Bicep/deploy scripts. Cloud Imaging Client and Media Builder ship from their own
release streams (tags `mse-ci-client-v*` / `mse-ci-mediabuilder-v*`).

### Drivers

A new **Drivers** page installs the vendor drivers for each device model during deployment. HP
and Dell business models are supported, for x64 and ARM64.

- **Onboarding**: pick models from the vendor's model list, preview each driver set, review the
  components and complete onboarding. Imaging Core downloads and verifies the files and builds
  driver set 1.
- **Sync**: Imaging Core reads the vendor catalogs on a schedule, on **Sync now** or on **Check
  for updates**, downloads new files, verifies them against the vendor's hashes and builds a new
  set when anything changed. New components can wait for approval.
- **Actions and rules**: each component is installed Offline, Offline and Specialize, Specialize,
  or skipped. Rules decide per category; an override per component wins. Categories marked
  critical fail the deployment when they cannot be installed.
- **Roll back** a whole driver set or one component, **Downloads** and **Storage** tabs, and
  **custom components** that add your own package or replace a vendor component on a model.
- **Sync progress**: a running sync or check shows a card on the **Sync** tab with each stage's
  count (vendor catalogs, models, components, driver sets), what it found so far and the latest
  changes.
- **Driver Synchronization report**: on the **Reports** page, for Readers, Operators and
  Administrators. Reliability, duration, changes per week, downloads and recurring failures over
  the last 90 days, with CSV export.
- **Devices**: the **Driver set** column shows the model each device matches for the chosen OS
  image, and anyone who can start imaging can choose another model or no drivers.
- **OS images**: set the Windows release on every OS image. Without it devices image without
  drivers.
- **Roles**: Operators and Administrators manage drivers. Technicians view them read-only.
- **Infrastructure**: redeploy the Template Spec, or run the upgrade script, to add the `drivers`
  blob container. Imaging Core creates its tables and queue itself. No data migration. Imaging
  Core must reach `hpia.hpcloud.hp.com`, `ftp.hp.com`, `ftp.ext.hp.com`, `downloads.dell.com` and
  `dl.dell.com` over HTTPS.
- **Upgrade order**: backend, then Media Builder `mse-ci-mediabuilder-v1.2.0`, then new boot
  images with Client `mse-ci-client-v1.2.0`. Devices on older boot images image without drivers.

See [Drivers](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/drivers.md).

### Security

- **Device session tokens**: the Device Gateway now checks every session request against the
  token Imaging Core stored when the session started, and refuses a token used for another
  session. Devices that are mid-session during the upgrade must restart from the boot media.
- **Custom component uploads**: packages are staged in a private location, checked against their
  declared size and hashed before they are stored. Only the operator who started an upload can
  complete, use or abandon it. Unused uploads are deleted after a day.
